title: Google Unveils TPU 8tx and 8i Max With AMD to Press Nvidia
excerpt: The 8tx pairs Google silicon with AMD EPYC processors for confidential computing, while the 8i Max doubles memory and compute for large AI workloads — both expected in 2027.
body:
• Google on Monday unveiled two specialised versions of its Tensor Processing Units — the TPU 8tx and the TPU 8i Max — stepping up its challenge to Nvidia in AI chips.
  • The 8tx pairs Google's silicon with AMD processors and hardware-level encryption for confidential computing, aimed at governments, banks and other regulated industries.
  • The 8i Max packs two TPU 8i chips into one package, doubling compute, SRAM and high-bandwidth-memory bandwidth for coding assistants, reasoning and drug-discovery workloads.
  • Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion in the September quarter, and the new systems are expected to become available in 2027.

Alphabet's Google introduced two new variations of its in-house Tensor Processing Units on Monday, according to Reuters, breaking from its traditional two-year launch cycle as demand for AI computing accelerates. The company is shifting toward specialised chips built for specific tasks rather than one general-purpose design. Google's head of chip development, Amin Vahdat, said the future of the AI industry lies in specialisation, India Today reported.

Two chips, two different bottlenecks

The TPU 8tx is built for confidential computing. It combines Google's 8t silicon with AMD's fifth-generation EPYC processors and hardware protection that keeps sensitive data and model weights encrypted while they are being processed — a requirement for government agencies, financial institutions and other customers in regulated industries. Google says the design delivers up to twice the speed of the previous version with virtually no performance trade-off, Reuters reported, while the company's own summary puts latency at up to 2× lower than the prior TPU 8t. Google Cloud executive Mark Lohmeyer said the partnership brings hardware-enforced confidential computing to cloud TPUs for the first time.

The TPU 8i Max takes the opposite approach: more raw capacity. It packages two 8i chips together, doubling compute, SRAM and high-bandwidth-memory bandwidth relative to the 8i, for workloads that need to hold very large amounts of information at once — coding assistants, mathematical reasoning and drug discovery among them.

Why AMD, and why now

The AMD partnership is the launch's most notable turn. Google introduced its TPU 8t and 8i systems in April using its own Axion CPUs, replacing the x86 processors used in earlier systems. For the 8tx, it turned back to an outside supplier — AMD — for the security capabilities its EPYC line provides. AMD says more than 10 major cloud providers and AI laboratories already use its EPYC processors alongside a range of AI chips.

The commercial backdrop is a cloud business growing at unusual speed. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% year over year to $30.7 billion in the third quarter, and Alphabet has said TPU sales made a meaningful contribution to the September quarter. Analysts cited by India Today estimate Google's TPUs cost roughly 30 per cent less than Nvidia's GPUs. Bloomberg Intelligence projects Google's TPU-related sales could rise from about $12 billion this year to more than $135 billion by 2028, though most of Google's new systems use its own Axion CPUs, so AMD would not benefit from all of that growth. Customers already lined up for Google hardware include Apple, Meta, OpenAI and Oracle, India Today reported, and Google is also expanding access through a partnership that will bring TPUs to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure in 2027.

What to watch

Both new systems are expected to become available in 2027, and the new designs have not yet been independently benchmarked. Independent testing of the previous Ironwood generation showed cost advantages in selected workloads, but results varied with the model, software and response-speed target — so the competitive picture against Nvidia will only settle once the 8tx and 8i Max are running customer workloads. Read the Reuters report via Global Banking & Finance Review.
